thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected in us-west-2 (streaming). Metric: service.streaming.generate.p99 = 1.8s (> SLO 1.0s). Paging oncall: @miguel (oncall) :rotating_light:

miguel (oncall): I'm on it. grabbing dashboard now. which model/cluster?

jules: seeing elevated tail on streaming in us-west-2 across several models, biggest for `redwood-open/gpt-large-v1` and a few quantized variants. p95 up 300ms, p99 up ~800ms.

ken: there are recurring ECC correctable errors on gpu-node-03a around the same timestamps from hw-monitor: `ce_count` spikes. tagging node: usw2-gpupool-03a.

maya (eng-runtime): confirmed. trace sampling shows stalls during KV cache fetch and some NVME page-in events prior to stalls. Could be GPU memory compaction/paging or ECC-induced micro-throttles.

miguel (oncall): what's customer impact? any 5xxs?

lina (support): No 5xxs reported from customers yet, but several streaming sessions reported stalls/`[connection stalled]` in user logs. One enterprise account (acme-corp) has elevated error emails to support. They've reported degraded streaming responsiveness.

jules: I can correlate request ids. Logs show repeated `CUDA_NONFATAL_ECC` and `SM_TEMPERATURE_THROTTLE` entries around the p99 windows. Looks like node had bursts of thermal throttle and ECC correctables.

devops-bot: NODE ALERT: gpu-node-03a reported temperature spike 86C at 3990000120, fan speed 4000RPM, ECC correctable errors increment +14. Auto-evacuate policy not triggered (threshold 20).

miguel (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) remove gpu-node-03a from scheduler pool (drain) 2) enable fallback routing to quantized-cpu fallback group for short-running streams 3) reduce batch sizes for streaming router in us-west-2 to limit tail amplification. I'll start 1 and 2 now.

maya (eng-runtime): agree. Also add prefix-KV cache bypass for live streams to avoid repeated GPU cache migrations (temporary toggle `runtime.kv_cache.streaming_bypass=true`). That reduces hot-cache thrash.

ken: initiating drain on gpu-node-03a: `kubectl cordon node/gpu-node-03a && kubectl drain node/gpu-node-03a --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — starting now. ETA for pod migration ~45s-2m depending on KV cache warmups.

jules: routing change in router config: switched 10% of traffic to dedicated-usw2-quant-cpu fallback and 90% to normal. Will ramp if p99 persists.

miguel (oncall): applied rate limit bump for bursty clients in us-west-2 (per-client concurrent streams cap from 8 -> 4) to avoid queue buildup while we drain.

lina (support): sending a proactive note to acme-corp: "We've seen transient streaming stalls in us-west-2; our on-call is mitigating and routing to fallback capacity. We expect recovery within 10-15 minutes. We'll update once the node is drained." Draft posted for review.

jules: after drain began, p99 dropped from 1.8s -> 1.05s within 90s. p95 back to baseline. Still seeing some 600ms tail spikes correlated with other nodes hitting transient ECC increments but nowhere near previous magnitude.

ken: node-level logs show ECC correctables increasing then stopping after drain. Thermal telemetry shows fan ramped but passive cooling insufficient. Hardware ticket queued: hw-ticket-8521 for follow-up and potential GPU replacement.

miguel (oncall): can we set auto-evacuate threshold lower to avoid manual paging next time? devops-bot said threshold is 20 correctables. consider lowering to 8 for this pool.

devops-bot: Proposed policy change: `auto_evacuate.threshold.correctables = 8` for gpupool-usw2; requires SRE approval and a short cutover.

maya (eng-runtime): We'll also add guardrails in runtime to reduce batch size when a node's CE rate > 2/min, to prevent p99 amplification. I'll open a PR for quick rollout with canary.

ken: hardware note: GPU temp sensor shows erratic readings on gpu-node-03a (possible sensor flake). If sensor is flaky may have caused spurious throttle events. We'll run stress test on node in maintenance window.

miguel (oncall): customer comms: Lina, please escalate to acme-corp with updated note that we drained the suspect node, p99 back near SLO, and we're performing hardware follow-up. Offer post-incident summary if they want.

lina (support): Sent update at 3990000205 to primary contact: "Node drained, mitigations active, monitoring for stability. We'll follow up with root-cause and timeline." They acked :thumbsup:.

jules: action items: - lower auto-evacuate threshold (ken) - runtime guardrail PR (maya) - hardware replacement ticket follow-up (ken) - postmortem doc (miguel/jules) - customer post-incident notes (lina).

miguel (oncall): I'll take on postmortem draft and timeline. For now, I'm handing off to next oncall: @jules is the responder for the ramp shift in 20m. If anything regresses ping me directly.

jules: taking responder handoff. Summary for next oncall: p99 spike caused by a mix of ECC correctable bursts and thermal/sensor anomalies on gpu-node-03a; live mitigations: drain node, route to quantized-cpu fallback, reduce per-client concurrency, temporarily bypass KV cache for streaming. Postmortem in `#incidents` doc to follow.

miguel (oncall): closing pager for me. leaving notes in ops-runbook under incident/3990000000.

devops-bot: NOTE: automation checklist: confirm drain completed (OK), verify p99 < 1.1s sustained for 10m (monitoring), schedule hardware investigation.

ken: drain completed at 3990000180. p99 steady at 0.98s for last 3m. I'll file the hardware RMA and schedule maintenance.

lina (support): customers notified, support queue showing no new escalations.

jules: marking incident as mitigated. We'll create a follow-up with timeline, telemetry, and RCA. Thanks team :tada:

incident-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated by action set { drain_node, fallback_routing, client_rate_limit }. Incident closed for pager: miguel (oncall).
